items.title: Retirement: Azure Communication Services (ACS) standalone services will be retired on September 30, 2028
items.description:
Microsoft will retire several standalone Azure Communication Services (ACS) offerings on September 30, 2028. After this date, the affected services will no longer be available.  

Details
Beginning September 30, 2028, the following ACS services will be retired and will no longer function: 

  • Email 
  • SMS 
  • Advanced Messaging with WhatsApp 
  • Chat 
  • Chat for Teams Meeting Interop 
  • Rooms 
  • Number Management (Direct Offer)
  • Direct Routing 
  • Job Router 
  • Web UI Library SDK 
  • Mobile UI Library SDK 

Several ACS services will also undergo breaking changes. These services will continue to function only when used with Microsoft Teams and will require customers to update their applications to the latest SDKs: 

  • Voice/Video Calling SDK 
  • Call Diagnostics 
  • Call Automation 
  • Audio Streaming 
  • Call Recording 
  • Closed Captions 

Standalone ACS calling implementations, or any implementation that does not update to the latest SDKs by September 30, 2028, will no longer be supported and will stop functioning after this date. 

Required action  

Review the ACS Retirement and Breaking Change FAQ to learn more. 

More information  

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, open the Azure portal and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

items.title: Generally Available: Instant Access for VM restore points
items.description:
Instant Access for application-consistent restore points on virtual machines (that have Premium v2 or Ultra disks as data disks) is now generally available. With Instant Access, you can begin restoring a disk from a restore point as soon as the snapshot is created, instead of waiting for the background data replication to complete fully. That shortens your recovery time objective when you are bringing a VM back online.

What's new at general availability

This release introduces “instantAccessState”, a consolidated read-only property on the restore point itself. During preview, customer had to inspect “snapshotAccessState” on each individual disk restore point and work out for themselves whether the restore point as a whole was usable. Now the customer can read one property at the restore point level and decide in a single step whether they can restore, copy, or download it, which removes per-disk polling logic from recovery automation and makes restore decision much simpler.

How to use it

Set instantAccess to true on the restore point collection to enable Instant Access for every restore point in it and optionally set instantAccessDurationMinutes on the restore point to control how long Instant Access stays active (60–300 minutes; the default is 300). Before you trigger a restore, read instantAccessState on the restore point and decide to restore based on its value rather than aggregating per-disk states yourself. 

Learn more.
